statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r equals the number of elements of A(nums), where A(nums) is the set of all positive integers g for which there exists a non-empty set I of indices such that I is a subset of {0, ..., len(nums)-1} and g is the greatest positive integer dividing nums[i] for every i in I. The cardinality is interpreted as a mathematical integer and then as the returned 64-bit integer.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 200000.

statement: The function returns a result r and does not fail (no panic, no out-of-bounds access, and no arithmetic overflow) for every input satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 200000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 1 <= r <= max{ nums[i] : 0 <= i < len(nums) }.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 200000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r >= |{ v : v is an integer and there exists i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = v }|.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 200000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= |{ d : d is a positive integer and there exists i with 0 <= i < len(nums) such that d divides nums[i] }|.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 200000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 1 if and only if there exists an integer v such that nums[i] = v for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 200000.

statement: If the function returns r on nums and returns r' on nums', then r = r'.
preconditions: len(nums) and len(nums') are each between 1 and 100000; every value of either slice is between 1 and 200000; and for every integer v, v occurs in nums if and only if v occurs in nums'.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, the following hold: if nums[0] = nums[1] then r = 1; if nums[0] != nums[1] and either nums[0] divides nums[1] or nums[1] divides nums[0], then r = 2; and if nums[0] != nums[1] and neither divides the other, then r = 3.
